Johann David Wyss, The Swiss Family Robinson, translated by Mary Jane Godwin and William Godwin, edited by Johann Rudolf Wyss.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/johann-david-wyss/the-swiss-family-robinson/mary-jane-godwin_william-godwin

People whose words are in the text, and their death dates:
- Johann David Wyss, annotator and author and writer of an introduction. Death dates in the facts file: 1818-01-11.
- Johann Rudolf Wyss, editor and writer of an afterword and writer of a preface. Death dates in the facts file: 1830-03-21.
- Mary Jane Godwin, translator. Death dates in the facts file: 1841-06-17.
- William Godwin, translator. Death dates in the facts file: 1836-04-07, 1836.

First publication of the text used: 1816 (English translation; the German original was published in 1812) (SE colophon: 'The Swiss Family Robinson was published in 1812 by Johann David Wyss. It was translated from German in 1816 by Mary Jane Godwin and William Godwin.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the edition's own rights statement (quoted below) says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication, and it does not matter here. Every death date listed for every person whose words are in the text is in 1925 or earlier (latest listed: 1841, Mary Jane Godwin). The text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
